GLUDICE.Settings.PhysicsEngine.Name: Physics engine
GLUDICE.Settings.PhysicsEngine.Hint: Which physics engine simulates the throws. Rapier is new and still being tested; cannon-es is the original Dice So Nice engine. Every client reloads when this changes.
GLUDICE.Notifications.RapierFallback: GLUniverse Dice: the Rapier physics engine could not start, so dice use cannon-es for this session. See the console for details.
GLUDICE.Settings.IdleRenderSkip.Name: Skip idle frames
GLUDICE.Settings.IdleRenderSkip.Hint: Stop redrawing the dice board while every die is at rest and you are not touching the mouse or keyboard. Saves GPU time while persistent dice sit on the table. Turn it off if dice on the board stop updating.
GLUDICE.Settings.ShaderPrewarm.Name: Prepare dice shaders at load
GLUDICE.Settings.ShaderPrewarm.Hint: After the world loads, build your dice once out of sight so the first throw does not stutter while the graphics driver compiles shaders.
GLUDICE.Settings.EnhancedMaterials.Name: Enhanced materials
GLUDICE.Settings.EnhancedMaterials.Hint: Richer versions of the built-in materials: a clear coat on plastic and wood, colour dispersion in glass and resin, denser velvet, brighter metal. Turn it off to render them exactly as Dice So Nice does. Needs realistic lighting.
GLUDICE.Settings.ImpactParticles.Name: Impact sparks
GLUDICE.Settings.ImpactParticles.Hint: Small sparks where dice hit each other and puffs where they hit the table, plus a burst around each die when it settles.
GLUDICE.Settings.SettleGlow.Name: Glow on the result
GLUDICE.Settings.SettleGlow.Hint: When the dice stop, the face that landed up glows for a moment, its number brightest, in the die's label colour. Not on d4.
